spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The PNT bridge is genuinely two-directional but asymmetric: zero-free boundary analyticity feeds a Tauberian theorem, while the prime asymptotic directly suppresses the error transform strongly enough to forbid a boundary pole.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Using -zeta'(s)/(s zeta(s)) as the Laplace transform of psi(e^t), Wiener-Ikehara and nonvanishing on Re(s)=1 give psi(x)~x; conversely psi(x)-x=o(x) makes (sigma-1) times its Mellin error transform tend to zero, contradicting the nonzero residue that a zero at 1+it would create.
directed.conceptual_reading: Analytic boundary regularity and arithmetic asymptotics are connected through a positive transform, with a Tauberian forward direction and a simpler Abelian-style converse.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge runs between the von Mangoldt cumulative function, its logarithmic-derivative Mellin transform, the pole at one, and zeros on the boundary line.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This establishes the PNT and its equivalence with nonvanishing on Re(s)=1 in the stated setting; it gives neither a quantitative error term nor information about zeros inside the critical strip.
directed.uncertainty: The transform sign and factor of s have minor extraction risk, and one prose line prints O(x) where the following epsilon argument uses the PNT consequence o(x).
